overall_reason: Every item is a bold rule name followed by a literal, checkable instruction ('<input> font size is ≥ 16px on mobile to prevent iOS Safari auto-zoom/pan on focus'), in the terse imperative docs register the page itself prescribes.

score.reason: T-RIVAL-NAME, T-THREE-LINE and T-TERMS pass on almost every item because each names a property, a number or a browser; only the intro's first sentence 'Interfaces succeed because of hundreds of choices' and one copywriting example fail. There are no section intros, no taglines and no claims to cut, which is what earns the score.

findings.title: Error copy that does not name the fix
findings.evidence: Failed T-STATE-COPY on the page's own example: 'Instead of "Your deployment failed," say "Something went wrong—try again or contact support."' The recommended line names neither what failed nor the cause, and the next rule on the page, 'Error messages guide the exit. Don't just state what went wrong—tell the user how to fix it', contradicts it.
findings.before: Something went wrong—try again or contact support.
findings.after: Make the example name the object and the next step, in the same form as the API key example below it: what failed (the deployment), why if known, and where to go (the build logs).
findings.why: A reader copying the first example ships the vague error the second rule forbids.

findings.title: Opening line that survives the rival's-name swap
findings.evidence: Failed T-RIVAL-NAME on one line: 'Interfaces succeed because of hundreds of choices.' would open any design guideline page. The sentences after it are the page's own ('a living, non-exhaustive list', 'some specific to React/Next.js').
findings.before: Interfaces succeed because of hundreds of choices.
findings.after: Open with the scope sentence that follows: what the list covers and for which stack.
findings.why: It is the first sentence a reader meets, and the only one on the page that carries no fact.

strengths: Each guideline is an imperative with a concrete property or number ('Set touch-action: manipulation', 'POST/PATCH/DELETE complete in <500ms', 'add a short show-delay (~150–300 ms)'); this exact docs register must not be softened by fixes.
The page marks its own scope honestly: 'These preferences reflect Vercel's brand & product choices. They aren't universal guidelines.'
Rule names are short assertions that work as an outline ('Don't block paste.', 'Links are links.', 'Never transition: all.').
not_investigated: T-LONG-FORM: ran on the one region the copy sheet lists (3 paragraphs, 95 words): 0 passive, 0 hedges, 0 vague attributions, 2 -ly adverbs; no finding. The page is a reference list, not running prose.
T-STATE-COPY on live states: no form on the page and async.json was not captured; only the example error copy in the text was judged.
Sweep: the repeated_label hit 'Instead of say .' comes from element text with the inline quoted examples stripped; bodyText shows the full examples, so it was not used as evidence.
T-TERMS: '10 MB' and '10MB' appear because the rule quotes the wrong form as its counter-example; 'AGENTS'/'agents' is the file name AGENTS.md; no finding.
Contract: no 00-contract.md in the run; judged as a Read (docs) page.
